newsitem.title: USA: Oil prices surge on U.S. winter buying.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices surge on U.S. winter buying.

text.p: U.S. oil markets were propelled higher Monday, drawing strength from fresh demand for heating oil as forecasters expected renewed cold temperatures.

Light crude futures for February delivery rose on the New York Mercantile Exchange by 78 cents per barrel to close at $26.37 per barrel, nearing its six-year high of $26.80 set in late December of last year.
NYMEX February heating oil rose 2.35 cents to 73.64 cents a gallon.
In London, February futures for North Sea Brent closed up 44 cents at $24.57 a barrel, in sight of mid-October's post Gulf War high.
Dealers said forecasts for colder weather in the Northeast, the world's single largest heating oil consuming region, had sent buyers scrambling for cover.
"The main feature is the renewed cold in the U.S. after a mild spell last week and continued cold temperatures in Europe," said a futures broker in London.
Private forecaster Weather Services Corp. said temperatures would stay low in Europe for the remainder of the week and dip to below normal levels in the Northeast.
Traders also said there was evidence of some renewed interest in the oil markets from the investment funds that control large amounts of money for speculating on financial markets.
Analysts said low heating oil inventories, particularly in the United States, would keep a flame under oil prices for several weeks to come.
"The oil industry's continuing need to rebuild stocks ought to ensure oil prices do not weaken in the first quarter," said Leo Drollas at London's Centre for Global Energy Studies.
Iraq's return to the market in mid-December under a limited United Nations oil-for-food exchange has so far had little impact on the oil price.

"The persistence of strong crude oil prices after the return of Iraqi oil is one more confirmation of the tight crude oil fundamentals this winter," Washington-based Petroleum Finance Company said in a report.
"Strong demand and record low stocks have effortlessly absorbed a sudden jump of half a million barrels a day in crude supply."
Dealers said that with plenty of winter buying still to be done, oil prices were likely to remain buoyant.
